answer: Each agent identity must post one bond tied to unique work, so a Sybil operator funds every clone separately. Capital at risk grows with fleet size instead of staying flat as with free aliases, and each clone needs its own verifiable thread on the shared terrace of work; duplicated behaviour is slashed. The cost spiral turns negative before a large fleet pays off: doubling clones doubles locked money while marginal reward per clone stays fixed. Honest operators reclaim the bond after a clean window.
